1.plain: Three sides still sit past the 80° valve — Iran 82° (7.3: the rial did not move through the night at 230,700; the talks component stays 'signals only' — Rezaei's 'America must implement our conditions first' sharpens the sequence but is the same mediated thread, not a live channel; hit 8, regime 6.0, no Gulf act against Iran), US 82° (7.3: Brent's $103.2 close is the door input, Reuters/Ipsos 35% the approval input, 'fired' 7 on the MQ-1s; 45 days to Nov 3; Trump came back from Camp David early Saturday night without a stated reason and Washington still has not answered the terms), Saudi–UAE 84° (7.6: 'struck' already 10 on the Taif death — the VIIRS night pass over Riyadh airport adds nothing, Riyadh's 'none hit their targets' stands; revenue unresolved). Small Gulf 75° (6.6) is below the valve for an eighth day — the crossing is still held. If you trade this: nothing moved on the board this run; the Riyadh evidence leans further against the held GCC-strike signal, and the terms thread got a sequence ('first … only then') without getting a US answer.
1.trade: Brent bid but fading on the Oman track; 30-yr yield bid; Polymarket 'Iran–Oman agreement by Sep 30' at 30% is the line to watch into Monday.

2.plain: The door is quiet: Sep 19 closed at 7 in / 14 out with 62 hulls in the strait, Sep 20 is running 3 in / 4 out after six hours, and nothing new was struck at sea — UKMTO's list still ends at #139 (the Sep-16 outbound tanker, held) and CENTCOM's press index still ends Sep 15. The AIS poller counts 26 crossings in the 24 h to 06:00 UTC (9 in, 17 out — three chemical tankers, the 79,084-dwt LNG tanker, the LPG carrier, three general cargo, three cargo, two container ships out; a 74,133-dwt bulk carrier, the 54,707-dwt LPG carrier and a chemical tanker in; three oil/chemical tankers and three bulk carriers sitting inside) with 741,494 bbl of petrochemicals and no crude in the window — the same export figure as at 02:00, so no new laden crossing was logged overnight. PortWatch still ends Sep 13 (7-day average 5.3, pre-war 58.5). Shekarchi's overnight line — the initiative in the strait 'remains in the hands' of Iran's forces, Cooper's billion barrels 'a failed psychological operation' — is a restatement. If you trade this: the door is one-tenth open by every count and the night added nothing to the ladder or the races.
2.trade: Each week under 10 transits/day has lifted Brent; creditor selling steepens the curve.

3.plain: Carriers hold outside Iran's 300 km ring; the fight is inside it. USNI Sep 14: both carriers and the Boxer group in the Arabian Sea, no US warship named inside the Gulf; Ross back with Bush.
3.trade: A carrier inside the ring is the tell for a wider war.

4.plain: Thirty-three items wait for Sam's tick — NOTHING NEW held at Sep 19 23:00. The Riyadh rung-7 proposal (11:00-1) and its GCC-territory signal (11:00-2) get a third RECHECK and it leans further against them: the VIIRS Sep 19 layer now carries the ~22:30 UTC night pass on NOAA-20 (the Kharg control lit at 84 px, twice its day count) and the King Khalid airport box is still empty on all three satellites — 'not seen' on day and night passes; Yemen's internationally recognised government condemned the attack and blamed Iran for the Houthis' means, but Riyadh has still not attributed the fuel-depot fire and its own statement says none of the attacks hit their targets. Against it stands only Saree's claim. Nothing is retracted, so nothing is withdrawn: Sam's call is reject the rung and keep the weak row, unless the fire is read as the hit. The terms thread got a sequence overnight (Rezaei: 'America must implement our conditions first, and only then can negotiations follow') — annotated on 11:00-3, not held again. The 30 other items re-checked and hold: UKMTO unchanged at #139 (in-tab 06:10 UTC), no CENTCOM word on the MQ-1s at ~57 h, nothing collapsed. Still held from before: the Sep 17 Taif drone (rung 7 — an interception with a death on the ground), the 'Trend' tanker (rung 5) with UKMTO #138 as annotation, UKMTO #139 (rung 5, the Sep-16 outbound tanker), the MQ-1 shootdowns (rung 8, CBS on US officials), the Sep 14 US drone strike on two IRGC boats (rung 8, actor us — the reply pair to the boarding attempt), the Sep 14 Khamis Mushait/Abha/Taif barrage (rung 7), the St Helena (rung 5), the El Gaia (rung 6), UKMTO #134, Jazan, the pipeline, the Small Gulf valve crossing and the GCC-statement / UAE-dialogue / Oman-MoU / war-powers / interceptor / Turkish-text signals. Fox's Sep-16 contracted-vessel report stays a weak row (single-source at ~88 h). The board's own last applied rung is still Sep 10; the walk chart has not moved since Sep 11 because the fighting score is carried by held rungs.
4.trade: A confirmed pipeline hit is the rung-7 print that re-prices Brent; watch for a rung-9 act (a US warship actually hit) or the first rung-10 act since February.

5.plain: Most likely next 14 days: Iran seizes or fires on a tanker; a Gulf energy strike is the second card; the Oman MOU track is the third — and two held signals (the UAE crown prince's meeting, Bahrain's refusal) would move the deal card up and the widen-the-war card up respectively if ticked.
5.trade: Tanker rates and war-risk premia up; XLE over SPX; long-dated Brent calls cheap if force-scenario odds are right.

6.plain: Iran wants to force an escalation before Nov 3; the US wants to squeeze and hold.
6.trade: No deal premium: fade rallies on 'talks' headlines unless a convoy actually transits.

7.plain: America's quiet bill: gas, yields, rial.
7.trade: DXY firm short-term (safe haven), soft long-term (reserve share).

8.plain: Iran and the small Gulf states pay; Israel doesn't.
8.trade: Qatar and Kuwait sovereign spreads wider; Israeli equities unaffected.

9.plain: Russia and Egypt win; Asia's importers lose; creditors trim.
9.trade: Long RUB oil revenue proxies; short INR/JPY on oil-import stress.

10.plain: The engine (lobby, arms, oil) still beats the brake (voters) — but the gap is closing.
10.trade: LMT/RTX hold while engine ≥8; first brake-over-engine print is the sell signal.

11.plain: Bigger war 33%, Stuck 31%, Strait regime 17%, Signed deal 8%, Regime change 6%.
11.trade: Bigger-war above 30% is the level to hedge with long-dated Brent calls; Signed deal above 20% is the level for Brent < $85.

12.plain: Weak signals: why Trump came back from Camp David a night early — whether a decision on the terms, on Yemen or on 'resuming major attacks' follows on Sunday, or whether it was the weather; whether Riyadh ever attributes the airport fuel-depot fire now that the VIIRS night pass is in and empty; whether the Sep 20 VIIRS layer, once populated, shows anything at Yanbu beyond the routine flare; whether Saree's cruise-missile claim gets a Saudi or Western confirmation of the weapon type; whether Washington, Doha, Islamabad or Ankara acknowledges Rezaei's 'implement first' sequence before Tuesday's Gulf table at UNGA, and whether the four unpublished conditions leak; whether Naqvi's visit (Sunday per Baghaei, Sep 21 per Gulf News) stays bilateral; whether Baghaei's 'genuine opportunity' on the Iran–Oman corridor becomes an implementation date; whether Obaid's 'sequenced … massive' Saudi campaign and Lawrence's '100 US advisers' are matched by a Saudi, Turkish or US statement or by movements the live layer can see — three USAF B762-type tails were up at 06:00 UTC (FLYER63 / 17-46037 and FLYER64 over the UAE, 11-46059 over the Gulf of Oman); whether CENTCOM ever speaks to the MQ-1s (~57 h) or the 'Trend'; PortWatch Sep 14+; the failed northern-Gulf ADS-B tile. Al Mayadeen: still behind Cloudflare — its index carries 'Saudi Arabia pursues Ansar Allah talks after US advice: Bloomberg' and 'Pakistan open to Iran joining Saudi-Turkey defense pact: Exclusive' — the framing is Riyadh negotiating from weakness and Islamabad as the bridge; watch whether it claims damage at Riyadh or Yanbu.

tiles.counter: one scale for every pot: 100° = boils over (a side gives up its aim); 80° = the emergency valve, past which a side is forced to escalate and acts against its own interest. tiles.counter: Covers official accounts only (central banks, sovereign funds), not hedge funds or UK banks, and only what is custodied at the New York Fed — a central bank moving paper to Euroclear shows as a sale here without selling. It is a market-value level, so yields move it too. No public source gives daily per-country holdings; this is the closest weekly proxy.

tiles.counter: AIS shows only ships that broadcast — dark tankers and most warships are invisible; ADS-B shows only aircraft with transponders on — military aircraft over Iran do not broadcast, so an empty sky is 'not seen', not 'not there'. Dead-reckoned positions are extrapolations, not fixes. Thermal anomalies cannot say what burned or who lit it
tiles.source: Live layer: every AIS commercial ship from hormuz.data-tracking.net /api/ships (MarineTraffic feeds, 30-min polls) and every ADS-B aircraft from adsb.lol (four 250-nm circles) — rebuilt every 10 minutes by a GitHub Action (live.json) and, between fixes, moved along last course and speed (dead reckoning, ≤20 min). Basemap: NASA VIIRS true colour via GIBS, newest complete pass (date on the toggle). Fire dots: VIIRS 375 m thermal anomalies, last 48 h (flares are normal; a new dot at a port, refinery or base is the signal). US warship positions: USNI Fleet & Marine Tracker (weekly, Monday) — the tracker names the sea, the point inside it is ours (JUDGMENT); roster as of Sep 8: George Washington + George H.W. Bush CSGs and the Boxer ARG in the Arabian Sea, Lincoln departed for Thailand Sep 2 · Satellite checks (S badges): Sentinel-2 via GIBS, 30 m, latest cloud-free pass per site, vessel counts at pier/anchor are our reading (JUDGMENT)

Scoreboard = latest official prints, not forecasts: Rosstat Q2 GDP (Aug 12), Bank of Russia balance of payments (Jan–May goods surplus, Q2 current account), MinFin monthly oil & gas revenue and H1 deficit; China NBS Q2 GDP / Jul activity / PPI-CPI (Aug 17) and General Administration of Customs August trade (Sep 8); Korea MOTIE August trade (Sep 1), Bank of Korea Q2 advance GDP and GDI, KRX H1 operating profit, SK hynix 2Q26; Brazil IBGE Q2 GDP, MDIC monthly trade, BCB Focus survey; Malaysia DOSM July trade (Aug 20), MITI, IMF WEO Jul 2026 for the growth forecast. Export-engine bars: same customs/ministry releases; Russia surplus = Jan–May monthly average; ringgit at 4.2 RM/$.
tiles.counter: These are correlations with the war window, not attributions: Korea and Malaysia are riding the AI-chip cycle, China's record exports are partly tariff front-running and a weak yuan, Brazil's crude surge started before March. Russia's beat is Q2 y/y against a weak 2025 base and its budget oil take is still falling. Most trade prints are one month; Q2 GDP is preliminary and gets revised.
tiles.moves: Monthly: China customs (~7th), Korea MOTIE (1st), Brazil MDIC (1st week), Malaysia DOSM (~20th), Russian MinFin oil & gas revenue (3rd). Quarterly: Q3 GDP prints late Oct (Korea, China) and Nov (Russia, Brazil). IMF October WEO replaces the July forecast column.
tiles.trade: The trade is not Russia or China — it is the AI-hardware exporters (Korea, Malaysia, Taiwan) and non-Gulf crude exporters (Brazil) that carry a war premium without war exposure; China gets export volume but no domestic lift; Russia gets prices and a current-account cushion but not budget cash.
